findings.title: Rush grade is free: standing still for 3 minutes earns A/A/A and is saved as the best medal
findings.problem: Arcade Rush ends on the clock. `complete()` is `game.time>=RUSH_TIME` (180 s), whatever the player did, so `win()` always fires at 180 s. The grade then comes from the shared Good Job formula: time 180 is under `limits.time` (190), so the time axis is always A. The overall grade is the best of the three axes, so every Rush run grades A. I proved it with a run where Pip never moves: no tray, no bench, zero cabinets. The result card shows a big gold A with a green check, "Orders served: 0", time 3:00 A, damage 0 A and cost 0 A. localStorage records `arcade-rush: {grade:'A'}`, and that best result counts toward the lobby bonus "Earn an A on three jobs". A full expert run with 32 cabinets also grades A, so the grade can't tell 0 cabinets from 32. Rush is a score-attack mode, and its only real score (orders served) isn't graded at all. Players lose the reason to replay and improve, the lobby medal is meaningless, and DR-07 is broken outright ("standing still … can't earn A on all three"). DR-38 is broken too: understanding is not rewarded.
evidence: mockups/review5/tools/arcade-rush-play/s4-idle.mjs log: idle 180.0 won true served 0, result A, saved best A
findings.fix:
Give rush levels their own grade. In `src/stations/types.ts`, add an optional `Station.grade?():{parts:Grade[];overall:Grade}`. In `src/game.ts:354`, use `this.station?.grade?.() ?? grade(...)`. In `ArcadeBench`, when `rush`:
- **Served axis** replaces time. Count only cabinets with tier ≥ 2: A ≥ 10, B ≥ 6, C ≥ 3, D below that.
- **Damage axis:** mistakes against 3.
- **Cost axis:** wasted credits only (see the cost finding).
- **Overall:** the served axis, capped one letter below by damage if damage > 2× the limit. Don't use best-of-three for rush.

If 0 cabinets were served, show a "Shift over: no orders served" fail card with the one-key retry (R), and don't call `record()`. In `src/ui/game-ui.ts:216-217`, replace the Time row with the Orders served row when `level.id.endsWith('-rush')`, as R3A N4 asked.
findings.verify: Add a test in tests/station-arcade-rush.spec.ts: open arcade-rush, `wait` 181 s with no input. Expect `won` (or the fail card) with an overall grade other than 'A', and localStorage to have no arcade-rush A. Re-run the clean spec (2 cabinets) and expect a grade of C or lower. Re-run the s2-clean.mjs expert run (32 cabinets) and expect A. Retake arcade-rush-play-40 and arcade-rush-play-26.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it. In v3-idle.mjs I never touched anything, and at t=180.0 the run showed won=true, served 0, damage 0, cost 0. The result card read 'A | Orders served: 0 | 3:00 A | 0 A | 0 A', and the 'Fuse tripped no more than once' bonus was also earned. localStorage then held circuit-crew:best:v1 = {"arcade-rush":{"grade":"A",...}}. In the code, complete() is game.time>=RUSH_TIME (station.ts:487), the rush time limit is RUSH_TIME+10 (station.ts:108), and the overall grade is the best of the three axes: grade.ts:6 sorts the parts and takes [0]. lobby.ts:46 counts bestFor().grade==='A'. This breaks DR-07 outright. The proposed fix is technically sound.

findings.title: The cost axis punishes success: every elegant sign-off adds credits, so 32 cabinets grade C on cost
findings.problem: Every sign-off adds that cabinet's parts to `spent` (`this.spent+=v.cost`). Rush caps cost at 24 credits. A cabinet's elegant fix uses 1–2 blocks, so a skilled player passes the cost limit at about 14 cabinets. My clean expert run served 32 elegant cabinets with zero mistakes and ended with cost 52, which grades C. Doing more, better work lowers a grade axis: the opposite of the bonus "Eight cabinets or more". In the story Arcade the parts cost is a fixed budget for five jobs. In Rush the job count is open, so a fixed cost cap is a penalty on throughput. A player who reads the result card learns "fixing more cabinets is bad". That teaches the wrong lesson and kills the score-attack loop.
evidence: mockups/review5/tools/arcade-rush-play/s2-clean.mjs log: cab31 … spent 52, mist 0, result cost C
findings.fix: In rush, charge only waste. At sign-off: `const waste=Math.max(0,v.cost-partsCost({chain:best(j)??[],reversed:false}));this.spent+=this.rush?waste:v.cost;`. Keep the pop charges at `station.ts:300` and `:308`, since those are real waste. Alternatively, scale the limit with the work done: `limits.cost = 3 + served*0.5`, computed at win. With the served-axis grade from the previous finding, cost becomes a secondary axis that rewards using the fewest blocks.
findings.verify: Run mockups/review5/tools/arcade-rush-play/s2-clean.mjs again. Expect cost to be 0 (the fixes are minimal) and the cost grade to be A after 32 cabinets. Add a unit test in src/stations/arcade/logic.test.ts or a station test: signing off best(j) adds 0 waste.
findings.verify_reason: The code confirms it. Every sign-off does spent+=v.cost (station.ts:273), and the rush cost limit is 24 (station.ts:107). In my v1 run, spent rose from 1 to 2 when I signed off a single 470 block. Shot 26 shows 52 credits graded C. The priority is too high, though. Because the overall grade is the best of three (grade.ts:6), the C on cost never lowers the overall grade or the saved medal. The 32-cabinet run still reads A. The C is a misleading signal on the card, not a lost reward, so P2.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-arcade-rush-play/v1-bench.mjs log: 'soak … spent 1' then 'after signoff … spent 2' (one 470 block charged at sign-off)
mockups/review5/shots/arcade-rush-play-26-result.jpg (cost 52 → C while the overall is still A)
findings.fix_correction: The waste-only charge works, but clamp it per cabinet against the cheapest tier≥2 chain, not only best(j). A player who signs off a different chain that is also minimal must not be charged. Keep the pop charges at station.ts:300 and :308. The cost axis only matters once finding 0 replaces best-of-three for rush. Without that change this fix has no effect on the medal.

findings.title: Swapping a block with the power on always trips the fuse, and the trip message lands on the new block
findings.problem:
To replace a block the player presses the position key to lift it, presses 1–4 to take a new one, then presses the position key again. While the block is lifted, the chain is "wire only". `update()` trips the fuse after 0.15 s live in a tripping state, and no human can do the three keypresses in under 0.15 s. So every live swap trips the fuse, counts a mistake and counts a fuse trip. My brute-force run on the first cabinet trips the fuse 5 times and counts 7 mistakes in about 15 s.

The bonus "Fuse tripped no more than once" is lost for anyone who experiments with the power on, which is the natural way to use a live meter. Worse, the toast for the wire-only trip ("Nothing in the chain limits the current: an LED straight across 9 V draws amps, so the fuse tripped.") stays up after the 100 Ω block is placed. In shot 33 the meter reads CHAIN 100 Ω and TRIP, next to a message saying nothing limits the current. A player concludes that 100 Ω trips a 9 V white LED's fuse, which is false: 59 mA is under the 100 mA fuse. This breaks DR-28 (the failure must show its real cause) and DR-19, and it makes experimenting expensive (A7, still open).
evidence: src/stations/arcade/station.ts:265 (slot with nothing held pops the block → empty position)
src/stations/arcade/station.ts:285 (fault counts mistake + trip once per arrangement)
src/stations/arcade/station.ts:437 (toast stays ≥4 s, not cleared on change)
mockups/review5/tools/arcade-rush-play/s3-wrong.mjs log: 'removed 47 live (wire only)' mis 2 trips 2 … '470 live' mis 6 trips 4
findings.fix:
Pick one of these. Option (a) is preferred.
- **(a) Auto-pause on lift.** In `act('slot')`, when a block is lifted while `this.powered` and the position becomes empty, call `this.powerOff()`. Animate the lever flipping back, play a soft clack, and say nothing. The prompt then reads "P Power on".
- **(b) Swap grace.** Add `private swapT=0`. Set it to 0.9 when a block is lifted while live, decrement it in `update()`, and skip the trip/pop/explain branch while `swapT>0 && this.held!==undefined`.

In both cases, hide the toast in `changed()` (`if(this.toast)this.toast.hidden=true`), so a message never outlives the arrangement it describes.
findings.verify: Script: with 470 Ω placed and the power on, press A, then 4, then A with 0.3 s between keys. Expect `snap().station.trips===0`, `mistakes===0`, and no toast. Retake shot 33: no 'Nothing in the chain' toast next to 100 Ω.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it at human speed. With 470 Ω live in play test, I pressed A, then 4, then A, 0.3 s apart. After the lift the fuse tripped (mistakes 1→2, trips 1→2). After the new 470 was placed, the toast still read 'Nothing in the chain limits the current…' while the meter showed CHAIN 470 Ω and TRIP (my shot 04). Four seconds later the board was live and in play test with 470 Ω (soak 0.6), and the same wire-only toast was still on screen. The claim that this happens 'always' is overstated. Placing the new block in another position before lifting the old one (2, then S, then A) swapped 470 for 100 with no trip. Only lifting the last block in the chain trips. Lifting and replacing in the same slot is still the natural swap, and the stale toast misattributes the cause (DR-28).
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-arcade-rush-play-04-after-live-swap.jpg (CHAIN 470 Ω + TRIP with the 'Nothing in the chain limits the current' toast)

mockups/review5/tools/verify-arcade-rush-play/v1-bench.mjs log: 'lifted live +0.3 … mis 2 trips 2'; 're-powered t 15.77 … 470 Ω … soak 0.6 … toast: Nothing in the chain limits the current'; 'swap via other slot (470->100) … trip false, trips 2'
findings.fix_correction: Option (a) is fine, but fire it only when the lift leaves the whole chain empty and nothing is across the LED. Removing one block of several is a legitimate live experiment. Also hide the toast in changed(), as proposed.

findings.title: The prompt tells the player to do the graded mistake: 'P Power on' on a broken start costs a mistake and a trip
findings.problem:
Several rush faults start with blocks already in the chain: 'hot' (47 Ω), 'dim' (470×3), 'backwards', and 'across'. For these, `prompt()` returns {key:'P',text:'Power on'}, because any position holds a block. A new player does what the one-line prompt says. On the first cabinet (white LED on 9 V with 47 Ω), pressing P trips the fuse within 0.15 s and immediately counts mistakes 1 and trips 1. The "fuse tripped no more than once" bonus is half spent before the player has made a single decision. The 'dim' start (470×3) fails silently after 0.6 s and also counts a mistake.

Powering up to see what is wrong is the diagnostic step the cabinet story invites ("Too bright, and the block smells warm"), but it is graded as damage. This is A7 from R4, still open, and the prompt now actively steers players into it. It breaks DR-19 (a prompt must be a real, good action) and DR-02 (only a mistake in the taught concept may be penalised; looking isn't a mistake).
evidence: mockups/review5/shots/arcade-rush-play-05-bench-first.jpg (prompt 'P Power on' on the 47 Ω fault)
findings.fix: Make looking free. In `showJob()` and after sign-off, store `this.startKey=JSON.stringify(this.setup)`. In `fault()`, return early without counting when `JSON.stringify(this.setup)===this.startKey`. Still show the trip and the explanation: that is the teaching beat. Keep counting once the player has changed the board. Optionally change the start prompt for broken boards to {key:'P',text:'Try it'}, so the first press reads as an inspection.
findings.verify: For each rush fault type (seeded jobs rush-0 hot, rush-1 dim, rush-6 across, rush-8 backwards from rng 20261029), press P at the start. Expect `snap().station.mistakes===0` and `trips===0`, with the toast and the TILT marquee still shown. Extend tests/station-arcade-rush.spec.ts.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it. At the first cabinet (rush-0, 47 Ω, white LED on 9 V) the prompt read 'P Power on'. Pressing P gave mistakes 1 and trips 1 within 0.4 s, with the toast '47 Ω lets 125 mA through: the fuse tripped.' The code path is prompt() at station.ts:485, then trip() and fault(true) at :288. The 'dim' and 'backwards' starts also count a mistake after 0.6 s through the tier-0 branch at :390. One detail is wrong: the 'across' start has an empty chain with a block across the LED, so chain.some(p=>p.length) is false. Its prompt is '1–4 Take a block', not 'P Power on'.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-arcade-rush-play/v1-bench.mjs log: 'cab0 start … prompt P Power on' then 'P as prompted … mis 1, trips 1, toast 47 Ω lets 125 mA through'
src/stations/arcade/logic.ts:213 ('across' start: chain empty, so the prompt is 1–4)
findings.fix_correction: The verify step should not expect 'P Power on' for rush-6 'across'. That start already prompts '1–4 Take a block'. The free-look check (setup equals startKey) still applies to it if the player presses P anyway.

findings.title: Phone (390×844): the bench is unplayable; two bins and the sign-off stamp are off-screen and there are no touch keys
findings.problem:
At 390×844 the bench camera keeps the desktop distance and FOV.
- The 47 Ω and 220 Ω bins are off the left edge; only slivers of the 100 and 470 bins show.
- The SIGN OFF stamp is off the right edge.
- The whole channel board is about 260 px wide, so the A/S/D pads and the ACROSS slot are about 15–20 px touch targets.
- The prompt pill shows keyboard badges ('P Power on', 'Esc Stand up') on a touch device with a virtual joystick and no keyboard.
- The toast covers the meter.

The bench's only inputs are hotkeys and 3D clicks, so a phone player can't take a 47 Ω or 220 Ω block or sign a cabinet off. No rush cabinet can be served on a phone. This is A12 / R3A M1, still open; Rush makes it worse because the mode is about speed. The RUSH panel also sits in the middle of the walking view on the phone start screen, just under Pip.
findings.verify: launch('arcade-rush',{width:390,height:844}), go to the bench, then take a screenshot: all 4 bins and the stamp are on screen, or the keypad is visible. Tap-drive a full cabinet with g.page.touchscreen.tap on the keypad until served.length===1.
findings.verify_reason: The layout problem is real, but it does not block play, so I downgraded it from P0. At 390×844 the 47 Ω and 220 Ω bins are fully off-screen. Only slivers of the 100 and 470 bins show at x≈0–40, and the SIGN OFF stamp is a few-pixel sliver at the right edge. In v5-phone-sign.mjs I fixed and served a cabinet using taps only: A pad (138,440), 470 sliver (12,470), A pad, lever (345,445), then the stamp sliver at (387,495), which gave served=1. 3D taps do work on touch, because pointerdown with button 0 reaches station.pointer. So 'no rush cabinet can be served on a phone' is false, and cabinets whose fix uses only 100/470 can be done. Any fix that needs 47 or 220 cannot be built, the targets are tiny, and the prompt pill shows keyboard badges and cannot be tapped (objectives.ts:93, no handler). The finding's code claim is also wrong. The bench camera does not keep the desktop distance: game.ts:372 already pulls back by clamp(1.25/aspect,1,2.1), and the 2.1 cap is what clips the 4.3 m bench. NEXT_STEPS.md:28-30 already lists this as a known gap.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-arcade-rush-play/v4-phone.mjs log: 'tap left-edge bin sliver 470', 'tap left-edge upper sliver 100' (47/220 unreachable)
src/game.ts:372 (an existing portrait pull-back, capped at 2.1×)
findings.fix_correction: Do not use distance*max(1,1.55/aspect). At aspect 0.46 that is about 3.4×, smaller than today's 2.1× cap, and it shrinks the pads to under 10 px. Keep the camera as it is and add the DOM keypad on (pointer:coarse): 4 candy bins, A/S/D, X, Flip, Power and Sign off, each at least 44 px and each calling act(). Or give the arcade a portrait-only view with lookX and a pitch closer to top-down, so the bins and the stamp move inside the frame. Hide the kbd badges in the prompt pill on touch, or make the pill tappable so it runs the prompted action.

findings.title: R at the bench instantly restarts the whole shift (and Space makes Pip jump mid-repair)
findings.problem: At the bench, `station.key()` handles only its own map. Every other key falls through to the walking handlers. KeyR calls `action('restart')`, which is `location.reload()` with no confirmation. R sits between E (stand up) and T, right next to the bench's F (flip), and the bench already uses 1–4, A, S, D, F, X, P, Enter and Backspace. Under rush time pressure a stray R wipes the run. In my test, 30.9 s and one served cabinet reset to t=0 and 0 served. Space also falls through: Pip jumps while seated (player y rose to 2.07 m, airborne 0.4) and Q tries to throw. A key should never destroy progress silently (DR-19), and the same key mustn't mean a different verb in the bench context (DR-22).
evidence: src/game.ts:164 (bench only consumes station keys, E and Esc)
mockups/review5/tools/arcade-rush-play/s3-wrong.mjs log: 'after R at bench 30.9 -> {t:0,…served:0}'; 'space at bench … player y 2.07 airborne .4'
findings.fix: In `src/game.ts:164`, while `atBench`, swallow every key that isn't a station key, apart from E, Esc and Tab, instead of falling through. For restart in timed rooms, require a 0.6 s hold of R with a radial fill on a small 'Hold R to restart' chip, or open the pause card with a Restart button. Leave R as a one-press retry only on the result and fail cards.
findings.verify: Script: at the bench mid-rush, press KeyR. Expect `snap().time` > 0 and served unchanged. Press Space. Expect `player.y` to stay near 0.77.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it. At the bench at t=29.6 with 1 served, pressing KeyR reloaded the page, and the snapshot after it showed t:0, atBench false, served 0. Space at the bench took player y from 0.77 to 1.92 with grounded false while atBench stayed true. In the code, game.ts:164 returns only for E, Esc and station keys. Other keys fall through to :166 (R restart, Space jump, Q throw), and restart is location.reload() at :178.

findings.title: The success moment is invisible from the bench: confetti, the lit cabinet and the cheering kid are all outside the bench camera
findings.problem:
Signing off a cabinet is the payoff of every 5-second rush loop, and from the bench view nothing physical happens.
- `cheer()` spawns the confetti 1.8 m behind the table, at about y 2.4, which is above and behind the meter and out of frame.
- `room.light()` relights a cabinet on the back wall, out of frame.
- The serviced cabinet and the play-test kid stand at x ≈ −2.95, off the left edge of the bench camera. Only a dark pink sliver shows.

So the kid's hop during the play test and the cheer when it passes, which were built as the station's main reaction, are never seen while working. At +0.1 s and +0.5 s after sign-off the frame shows only a toast ('Dance: Elegant ★') and a reset board. Rush repeats this 10–30 times, and each completion lands as a text pill. This breaks DR-11 (juicy success with flash, sound and hitstop, the machine in frame) and DR-47 (the device shows its state on itself).

mockups/review5/shots/arcade-rush-play-36-bench-cabinet-kid.jpg (cabinet + kid only visible after standing up)
src/stations/shared.ts:11-14 (bench confetti 1.8 m behind the table)

findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it. In bench-view shots at sign-off +0.1 s and +0.4 s, nothing in frame reacts except the toast 'Dance: Elegant ★' and the reset board. A single confetti chip shows over the meter. The serviced cabinet and the kid are not in frame (only a pink sliver at the far left). The code confirms why: cheer() at the bench places the burst 1.8 m behind the table at y+1.4 (shared.ts:11-14), the cabinet stands at table.x+OX−2.75 (station.ts:215), and the bench view has no lookX (station.ts:80).

findings.title: No escalation: Rush is the same number-match loop 30 times with about nine answers
findings.problem:
`rushJob()` only makes single-LED cabinets.
- **Variety:** 4 colours, supplies of 3.3/5/9/12 V, 3 current bands, and 5 one-shot faults.
- **No other kinds:** there are no battery-life cabinets, no transistor-base cabinets, and no combined faults. Every cabinet uses the same pink bench cabinet model.
- **Few answers:** in the 32-cabinet run, the elegant fixes collapse to about nine chains: 470; 220; 470+470; 220+470; 47+220; 100+220; 220‖470; 47+47; 100. Many repeat back to back (white 9 V → 470 three times).
- **'backwards' gives the answer away:** the job starts with the correct chain already in place, and the story says it is backwards, so the whole job is pressing F.
- **Flat loop:** each cabinet takes about 5 s (2 s to read, 1–7 keypresses, 2 s soak). Difficulty, pace and stakes never change across the 180 s, and the world never changes: no queue of kids, no cabinets crowding the bench, no rising tension.

After about 5 cabinets a player is matching a lookup table, not reasoning about I = (V − Vf) ÷ R. R4B's redesign ideas for the arcade (kid queue, blocks popping across the room, a battery time-lapse, A6) were NOT BUILT. For a mode whose whole point is replay, this is the main fun problem.
evidence: src/stations/arcade/logic.ts:200-221 (rushJob: LED only, five single faults)
findings.fix:
In `src/stations/arcade/logic.ts`:
- **Escalate by `n`:**
  - n < 3: today's single faults.
  - 3 ≤ n < 7: combined faults (reversed + hot, across + dim).
  - n ≥ 7: mix in the story's `handheld` battery kind (life target, `battery:true`) and the `hopper` base kind (`load.kind:'base'`; the bench already draws the transistor and motor).
- **Narrower bands later:** for example [.012,.016], where only a parallel pair lands in the ★ zone.
- **No back-to-back repeats:** don't repeat the same best() chain twice in a row (keep the last fix, re-roll on a match).
- **'backwards':** start it with a near-miss chain (one block wrong) plus the reversal.

In `station.ts` / `room.ts`:
- Show a queue of 1–3 blob kids at the bench's left end. A new one joins every 20 s, and they groan and leave after 30 s, which costs a 'walkout'.
- Vary the serviced cabinet's body colour and marquee per title, using `cabinet()` from `room.ts`.
- Add a streak multiplier (3 elegant in a row → a ticket burst).
findings.verify: Add a unit test in logic.test.ts: over 60 rushJob(rng(11),n), at least 2 load kinds appear after n ≥ 7, no two consecutive best() chains are equal, and every job still has best(). Re-run s2-clean.mjs and confirm the cabinet list shows battery and transistor cabinets and combined faults.
findings.verify_reason: The code confirms the claim. rushJob (logic.ts:204-221) only builds led() loads, with 4 colours, 3–4 supplies, 3 bands and 5 single faults. Nothing scales with n. 'backwards' starts with best(j) already in place and reversed (logic.ts:214), so pressing F alone solves it. I did not re-run the 32-cabinet list, so 'about nine answers' rests on the reviewer's log. It is plausible given the 4 block values and the 2-per-position limit. The suggested battery and base kinds are real: the bench already toggles the transistor and motor (station.ts:242).
extra_evidence: src/stations/arcade/station.ts:242 (the bench already renders base/transistor jobs)

findings.title: The chaos shortcut is punished: a tray thrown onto the bench lands there but doesn't count, and it's graded as damage
findings.problem:
The only physical job act in Rush is carrying the resistor tray to the bench. The obvious Good Job shortcut is to throw it. I threw the tray (Q) from about 3 m away. It landed on the bench top at (−1.74, 1.07, −1.85), inside the 2.6 m acceptance radius of the table, but `trayReady` stayed false. `station.dropped()` is only called from the E-drop path in `interact()`, never on landing.

The throw also counted as damage: the HUD went to damage 1 and cost 10, because the job item hit the bench at more than 5.5 m/s. After the throw the card still says 'Carry the tray…' while the tray visibly sits on the bench. The prompt points at a nearby prop ('E Grab the paper'), not the tray, so a new player thinks the game is broken. Clean first and chaos second means the chaos route has to work too (DR-01), and chaos mustn't fail or cost the player (DR-02).
evidence: mockups/review5/shots/arcade-rush-play-52-tray-thrown.jpg (tray on bench, card unchanged, damage 1, cost 10)
src/game.ts:209-210 (station.dropped called only from the E-drop branch)
src/game.ts:335 (impact damage counts job items too)
mockups/review5/tools/arcade-rush-play/s5-chaos.mjs log: 'tray after throw … trayReady false dmg 1'
findings.fix: In `ArcadeBench.update()`, while `!trayReady`, check every frame whether the tray body is within 2.6 m of `table`, its speed is under 0.6 m/s and it isn't held. If so, run the same acceptance as `dropped()`, plus a 'Nice throw!' confetti burst and the jingle. In `src/game.ts:335`, skip impact damage for props with `spec.id` (job items), or at least for 'blocks' landing on the bench. Add a bonus to the rush and story bonus lists: 'Throw the tray onto the bench'.
findings.verify: Re-run mockups/review5/tools/arcade-rush-play/s5-chaos.mjs. After the throw, expect `snap().station.trayReady===true`, `damage===0`, and the card advanced to 'Step up to the service bench'. Retake shot 52.
findings.verify_reason: The code confirms it. station.dropped() is called only from the E-drop branch (game.ts:210), and the Q-throw path (game.ts:183) never calls it. Reviewer shot 53 clearly shows the tray resting on the bench top while the card still reads 'Carry the tray…'. My own throw (v2-throw.mjs) did not land on the bench. The tray hit the serviced cabinet and settled on the floor at (−2.75, −1.13), 3.05 m from the table. It also counted damage 1 and cost 10 at +0.25 s. After that, sitting at the bench gave the prompt 'E Fetch the resistor tray' with trayReady false. The physical shortcut never counts. The damage part works as designed: the Good Job damage bill is what DR-07 grades chaos with.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-arcade-rush-play/v2-throw.mjs log: 't+ 0.25 … dmg 1 cost 10 trayReady false'; 'sit true trayReady false … prompt E Fetch the resistor tray'
findings.fix_correction: Do the per-frame acceptance in ArcadeBench.update(), as proposed. Do not exempt all job items from impact damage in game.ts:335: that removes chaos cost across every room and works against DR-07. At most, skip the damage when the tray's impact is the acceptance landing on the bench top (y≈1 and within 2.6 m of the table).

findings.title: No cable anywhere in Rush, and the action bar still offers a plug (F) and a slingshot (Q) that do nothing
findings.problem: AGENTS 4 says the cable is the star in every playable room. In arcade-rush the rope isn't simulated or drawn (rope maxLength 10 exists, but `game.ts:104` skips it for stations). The room's only physical act is a 6-second tray carry, and everything after that happens in a menu-like bench view. Meanwhile the walking HUD action bar shows the F 'plug' button and the Q 'slingshot' button (greyed) on every walking frame. They are false affordances: F does nothing (`cableReady=false` for stations) and there is nothing to slingshot. A new player who presses F gets a shrug puff. DR-05 already knows the station rooms have no cable; Rush makes it worse, because the shift is pure bench time.
evidence: mockups/review5/shots/arcade-rush-play-01-start.jpg (action bar with F plug and Q slingshot)
src/game.ts:92,104 (cable hidden and not simulated for stations)
src/ui/game-ui.ts:185-195 (cable button state for stations: ready=false but still shown)
findings.fix: Short term: in `src/ui/game-ui.ts` `updateActions()`, hide the F and Q action buttons (`el.hidden=true`) when `g.station||g.hub` has no cable. Design fix: give the bench a short power lead (for example 6 m) that Pip must plug into a wall socket at shift start. Reuse the playground rope with `level.length`, an anchor at the bench and a target socket on the back wall at (−3,−7.6). Strain colours show if Pip wanders, and a yank (slingshot) unplugs the bench as harmless chaos: the power drops and the kids groan, with no mistake counted.
findings.verify: Start shot: no F or Q button in a station room (or a visible bench lead). If the lead is built, `snap().rope.maxLength>0` and the cable is drawn at the game camera.
findings.verify_reason: The code confirms it. The rope, plug, anchor and target are hidden for stations (game.ts:92), and simulateCable is skipped (game.ts:104). levels/types.ts:13 says station jobs 'have no cable of their own', a known DR-05 gap. Pressing F with nothing in hand reaches shrug() at game.ts:220. The action bar keeps the F button looking normal, because cable.off is only set while holding (game-ui.ts:199). Only Q is greyed (shot 52). This duplicates the known DR-05 gap, but the false F affordance is real.
extra_evidence: src/ui/game-ui.ts:196,199 (cableReady false for stations; off only when holding)

findings.title: Bench mistakes are invisible until the result card: the HUD damage tally reads 0 while mistakes climb to 7
findings.problem: Station mistakes (fuse trips, tier-0 runs, pops) are added to `game.damage` only inside `win()`. During the whole shift the HUD damage tally reads '0' and stays hidden, even when `station.mistakes` is 7 and `trips` is 5. The player gets no running signal that their experiments are graded, until the result card at the end. That breaks the Good Job loop of seeing the bill tick up. It also hides the cause of the lost 'Fuse tripped no more than once' bonus, except through a tiny star colour on the job card.
evidence: src/game.ts:353 (mistakes added to damage only at win)
findings.fix: In `src/ui/game-ui.ts:165`, display `g.damage+(g.station?.score().mistakes??0)` and `g.cost+(g.station?.score().cost??0)`, so the tallies pop as they rise. Also give the bench fuse a visible tally: a small row of 3 pips on the fuse plate that turn red per trip, matching the bonus.
findings.verify: At the bench, trip the fuse once. The HUD damage tally appears with '1' and animates. Screenshot crop of the HUD.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it. After the prompted P trip (mistakes 1, trips 1), the HUD tallies were 'tally:true:0 || tally:true:0', meaning the damage and cost boxes stayed hidden at 0. They stayed that way through mistakes 3. g.damage only gets station mistakes inside win() (game.ts:353), and the tallies read g.damage and g.cost (game-ui.ts:165).
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-arcade-rush-play/v1-bench.mjs log: 'hud tallies tally:false:2:53 || tally:true:0 || tally:true:0' with mis 1, and tally '2:32 / 0 / 0' at mis 3
findings.fix_correction: When showing g.damage+station.mistakes live, stop adding once g.won is true. win() already folds the mistakes into g.damage (game.ts:353), so a naive sum would show double on the result frame. Alternatively, have win() stop adding them and always show the sum.

findings.title: The clock gives no grace: an order mid play-test at 0:00 is simply lost
findings.problem: When `game.time` reaches 180, `current()` returns undefined, `complete()` is true and `win()` fires on the same frame. In my expert run, the 33rd cabinet was at 'PLAY TEST 1.8 / 2 s' when the clock hit zero. The win push-in shows that unfinished play test frozen on the monitor, and the cabinet is not counted. Losing an almost-finished order to a hard cutoff reads as unfair. Overcooked-style rush modes let the last order land, or at least show a 'last order' warning. There is also no countdown juice: no red clock, no ticking and no 'LAST 10 SECONDS' marquee.
findings.fix: In rush, if `powered && soak>0 && !soakDone` when the time reaches RUSH_TIME, allow up to `RUSH_SOAK` seconds of overtime. `complete()` returns `time>=RUSH_TIME && !(this.soak>0&&!this.soakDone&&time<RUSH_TIME+RUSH_SOAK)`. If the soak passes, auto-sign it with the 'LAST ORDER!' marquee. Under 30 s, turn the HUD clock red with a scale pulse and add a soft tick every second under 10 s (R3A N4 asked for red under 30 s).
findings.verify: Script: start a correct cabinet at t = 179.0 and advance 3 s. Expect served to include it and `won` true at about 181 s. HUD crop at 25 s left shows the red clock.
findings.verify_reason: The code and the screenshot confirm it. current() returns undefined at game.time>=RUSH_TIME (station.ts:127), and complete() fires on the same frame (station.ts:487). Shot 25 shows the monitor frozen at 'PLAY TEST 1.8 / 2 s' at the win push-in. The HUD only toggles .late when time > level.deadline (game-ui.ts:167, default 240), so the rush clock never gets any urgency styling. Losing one order at the buzzer is a fairness and polish issue, not a noticeable loss of fun or teaching, so P2.
findings.fix_correction: Changing complete() alone is not enough. current() returns undefined once time ≥ RUSH_TIME, so update() skips the soak, act('signoff') returns false and the panel hides. current() must keep returning the job in progress during the overtime window, e.g. `if(this.game.time>=RUSH_TIME&&!(this.soak>0&&this.game.time<RUSH_TIME+RUSH_SOAK))return undefined;`. Then auto-sign it.

findings.title: The tall storeroom shelf hides Pip and the tray, with no occlusion fade
findings.problem: The resistor tray (the one required item) lives in the storeroom. When it is near the 2 m stock shelf at (−9.6, 7.2), or when Pip stands between the shelf and the back wall, the shelf sits between the camera and Pip. Pip shows only as a hat sliver behind the pastel stock boxes, and the tray on the middle level is nearly hidden. The shelf doesn't fade, because only pillars are registered as occluders. In the same frame the floating STOREROOM sign is still there (DR-72, known, still open).
findings.fix: Register the storeroom shelf group, and the `store-a` and `store-b` interior walls, with the occluder fade list used for pillars (see `src/levels/decor.ts:55` and the fade loop at `src/game.ts:386-388`). Fade to opacity ≤ 0.25 within 0.2 s. Cast rays to Pip's feet, chest and head and to the current step's `at()` (the tray). Mount the STOREROOM plaque on the store-b wall face at z ≈ 2.76, y 1.2, rather than floating at 2.1.
findings.verify: Take a zoom-9 shot with Pip behind the shelf (walk to (−9.3, 6.5), then orbit ±200). At least 70% of Pip's pixels are visible and the shelf is faded. Orbit 90° and 180° around the plaque: it sits flush on the wall.
findings.verify_reason: The code confirms that the storeroom shelf (room.ts:111-113) is a plain group plus a solid collider and is not in game.occluders. Only shell walls and decor.ts pillars are (decor.ts:48,55). The 'Pip shows only as a hat sliver' claim is overstated, though. In shot 58, Pip's hat, face, arm and the tray are all visible through the open shelving. The occlusion also only happens when Pip wanders north of the shelf (z<7.2) with the camera zoomed in. The spec route to the tray counter at (−9.2, 4.3) never goes there, and at default pitch the sightline clears the 2 m shelf. The STOREROOM plane floats at y 2.1 (room.ts:115), matching the known DR-72. It is a minor DR-12 violation off the main route, so P2.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/arcade-rush-play-58-tray-after-shelf-10s.jpg (Pip and the tray mostly visible through the shelf gaps)
src/levels/decor.ts:48,55 (only walls and pillars push to occluders)
findings.fix_correction: Registering the shelf meshes as occluders requires cloning their materials with transparent=true. The fade loop at game.ts:388 mutates material.opacity, and toon() materials may be shared caches, which would fade every mesh using that colour. Also, the fade ray only targets Pip's chest (game.ts:387). Extending it to the tray means a second ray toward the current step's at().

findings.title: Two clocks that disagree: the HUD ring measures 240 s while the clock counts down 180 s, and the panel repeats the seconds
findings.problem: The HUD's bell ring uses `g.level.deadline ?? 240`, and Rush has no deadline. At 9 s left the clock reads 0:09 while the ring still shows about 30% remaining. At 0:00 the ring is still a quarter full. The station panel header repeats the countdown as 'RUSH · 138 s · 7 fixed' next to the HUD's '2:17': the same value twice in different formats (DR-41). R3A N4 flagged two clocks for Via Rush. Here the clock direction was fixed, but the ring and the duplicate remain.
findings.fix: In `game-ui.ts:166`, use `rush ? rush.left/RUSH_TIME : 1-g.time/deadline` for the ring (expose `total` from `rushStatus()`). In `station.ts:449`, drop the seconds from the header and keep the served count prominent: '7 fixed · CLAW'.
findings.verify: HUD crop at t = 170: the ring is about 5% and matches 0:09. The bench panel header has no seconds.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it. At t=171.5 the HUD clock read 0:08 while the ring's stroke-dasharray was 66.4 of 232.5 (29% left), because it is computed from deadline ?? 240 (game-ui.ts:166). The panel header repeats the seconds ('RUSH · 174 s · 0 fixed') next to the HUD's 2:53 (station.ts:449), which breaks DR-41.

findings.title: The result card's time row is always 3:00 A, and Orders served is a small caption
findings.problem: R3A N4 asked for the time row to be replaced by an 'orders served' row on rush levels. Today the card still shows the full-width time row '3:00' with an A medal, which is the same on every run, and adds 'Orders served: 32' as a small line under the medal, the same size as the bonus list. The number the player played for is the least prominent thing on the card. This is a partial regression of R3A N4.
findings.fix: In `resultMarkup` (`src/ui/screens.ts`) or `game-ui.ts:217`, when `level.id.endsWith('-rush')`, render the first row as a ticket icon, the served count (count-up) and its own letter from the served-axis grade. Remove the time row. Show 'best: n' from the record next to it.
findings.verify: Retake the result shot after the s2-clean run: the first row reads '32' with a ticket icon and a medal, and there is no 3:00 row.
findings.verify_reason:
The screenshots and the code confirm it. Shots 26 and 40 show a full-width time row '3:00 A', and the result card inserts 'Orders served' as a small

before the rows (game-ui.ts:217). In shot 25 it is also the only text visible before the rows land. Because the time row is identical every run, the card conveys no rush information.

findings.title: Stale text: the card lags at the bench, and old toasts describe arrangements that no longer exist
findings.problem: On sitting down, the job card keeps 'Step up to the service bench (E)' for about 0.8 s, while the prompt already says 'P Power on'. More importantly, toasts live at least 4 s and aren't cleared when the board changes. At '470 live', the chain is 470 Ω and in play test, but the toast still reads 'Nothing in the chain limits the current…', so the player reads a failure over a passing setup. After sign-off, the next cabinet's first frame still shows the previous cabinet's 'Dance: Elegant ★' toast, and it is still on screen after standing up and opening the survey.
evidence: mockups/review5/tools/arcade-rush-play/s3-wrong.mjs log: 'cab0 start' card 'Step up…' while atBench; '470 live' toast 'Nothing in the chain…'
findings.fix: Hide the toast in `changed()` and in `setActive(false)`. Shorten sign-off toasts to 1.6 s. In `src/ui/objectives.ts`, update the card on the same frame that `active` turns true (don't throttle latching for steps whose `done()` turned true this frame).
findings.verify: Script: trip, then fix within 1 s; the toast is hidden once the setup changes. Card text equals 'Fix cabinets…' within 0.1 s of pressing E at the bench.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it. 0.5 s after sitting down, the card still read 'Step up to the service bench (E)' while the prompt was 'P Power on'. After sign-off, the next cabinet (RACER) showed 'Dance: Elegant ★' as the toast in both shots 06 and 07. The wire-only toast also survived two board changes and a re-power (see finding 2). changed() leaves the toast alone (station.ts:247), and say() keeps it at least 4 s (station.ts:437).
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-arcade-rush-play/v1-bench.mjs log: 'cab0 start … card Step up to the service bench (E) … prompt P Power on' while atBench

findings.title: The bench shows key letters on the pads but not on the bins, the lever or the stamp
findings.problem: The board prints A/S/D under the chain pads and X beside ACROSS. The four bins carry their Ω values but no 1–4 keycap, the POWER lever has no P, the SIGN OFF stamp has no Enter mark, and the LED has no F. On a 'hot', 'dim', 'across' or 'backwards' start the prompt skips straight to 'P Power on', so the player never sees the '1–4 Take a block' prompt. Learning the 12-key layout depends on hovering with the mouse. For a speed mode, keys need to be readable at a glance. R3A N3 recommended a shared `benchKey()` keycap; it isn't used here.
evidence: src/stations/arcade/station.ts:190-211 (bins, lever, stamp with no keycap)
findings.fix: Add small cream keycap plates (`sign()` with a 0.06 m plate) to each bin rim ('1'…'4'), the lever base ('P'), the stamp rim ('⏎') and the LED rim ('F'). Use the same style as the A/S/D legends, at least 14 px cap height at 1440×900.
findings.verify: Bench crop: each control shows its key. Measure cap height ≥ 14 px.
findings.verify_reason: The screenshot confirms it. The bins show only their Ω values, the lever has no P, the stamp shows only a ✓, and the LED has no F. Only A/S/D and X are printed on the board (station.ts:529). Hover hints (station.ts:460-468) do show the key, but only when the mouse is over a control.

findings.title: The tray fetch and 'step up' eat about 6.5 s of the rush clock every run, repeating the story level
findings.problem: The rush clock is `game.time` from spawn, so the storeroom fetch, the carry and sitting down (about 6.5 s, or 11 s for a player who looks around first) all come off the 180 s shift. A player who has already finished the Arcade repeats the same chore every rush attempt before any scoring starts. It is short, but it is pure overhead on every retry, which matters most in a replay mode (DR-20: retries should be cheap). The objective card for these steps is also the long 'Carry the tray of resistor blocks from the storeroom to the service bench' sentence (DR-39 and DR-40).
findings.fix: Either start the rush clock at the first `setActive(true)` (`rushStart=game.time`; use `game.time-rushStart` in `current()`, `complete()` and `rushStatus()`, and show 'READY?' on the HUD until then), or, in rush only, start with the tray already delivered (`trayReady=true`, bins visible) and Pip spawned at the bench stand. Shorten the step text to 'Bring the resistor tray to the bench'.
findings.verify: snap() at first sit: rushStatus().left === 180. Or, with the pre-delivered tray, the first-frame shot shows the bins on the bench.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it. The scripted fetch and seat took 6.0 s of the rush clock, and the first sit came at t=6.5, with the panel already at 174 s. The clock is game.time from spawn (station.ts:127,487,489).
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-arcade-rush-play/v1-bench.mjs log: 'toBench true true t 6.5 leg 6.0', panel 'RUSH · 174 s'

findings.title: Back-wall cabinets light by index % 5 from the story jobs, and every rush sign-off stacks another glow and confetti burst on them
findings.problem: `act('signoff')` calls `this.room?.light(this.index%5)`, and `light()` creates a new glow sprite (opacity 0.35) plus 16 confetti on the story cabinet k: PINBALL, RHYTHM, CLAW, HANDHELD, PRIZES. In Rush, the fixed cabinets are DANCE, RACER, SKEE and so on, so the wrong marquees light up. After five sign-offs every one is lit already, and each later sign-off stacks another glow sprite on the same marquee. A 32-cabinet run adds about 27 redundant additive sprites at the back wall. That breaks the restrained-glow rule over time and leaks objects. Visually at 12 cabinets it is still modest, but it grows without bound.
findings.fix: In `room.ts` `light(k)`, return early if `lit[k].done`, and set `done=true` the first time. In rush, light the back-wall cabinets as a progress meter instead: cabinet k lights at served = 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, with its marquee retitled to the rush cabinet just fixed. Or add a 'FIXED' tally board on the back wall, a canvas plaque redrawn per sign-off.
findings.verify: After 32 sign-offs, count the sprites added by light(): there are 5. Survey shot: marquees show rush titles or a progress meaning.
findings.verify_reason: The code confirms it. Sign-off calls room.light(index%5) (station.ts:276). light() adds a new glow sprite (opacity 0.35) and a 16-piece confetti burst on every call with no guard (room.ts:122-123). lit[] holds the five story cabinets (PINBALL, RHYTHM, CLAW, HANDHELD, PRIZES) from room.ts:84, not the rush titles. I did not count the sprites after 32 sign-offs, but the growth without bound follows directly from the code.
extra_evidence: src/stations/arcade/room.ts:81-84 (lit[] built from the story JOBS titles)

findings.title: Draw calls are about 5.6× over budget in Arcade Rush
findings.problem: `snap().drawCalls` is 1416 at the game camera on start, 1491 in the survey and 1178 at the bench view. The budget is about 250 (DR-24). This is A13 (1181 in R3B), still open and slightly worse. Rush is a speed mode played on the same dense arcade (132 props plus cabinets), so frame hitches during fast key input hurt directly. The fps reading in ?manual mode isn't reliable (31 at start, 60 in survey), so this needs a real-time check, but the draw-call count alone fails the rule.
evidence: mockups/review5/tools/arcade-rush-play/s1-start.mjs log: dc 1416 start, survey dc 1491, bench dc 1178
findings.fix: Merge the static arcade decor the way Lunch was merged (from 1090 down to about 175): run the cabinets from `cabinet()`, the shelf, the counter, the bench body and the clutter through the static merge into `decorRoot`. Keep only clickables and animated parts (LED, fuse, lever, kid, coin) as separate meshes. Instance the clutter boxes, cones and beanbags by kind.
findings.verify: `snap().drawCalls` ≤ 250 at start and ≤ 300 at the bench, plus a real-time fps ≥ 50 measured without ?manual.
findings.verify_reason: The draw-call counts reproduce: drawCalls was 1491 at the first manual frame and 1178 at the bench (v1). Without ?manual it was a steady 1416 at the game camera (v6). That is over DR-24's ~250. But real-time play on the host GPU held 60 fps, with draw at ~4.9 ms and step at ~0.2 ms (v6-fps.mjs). So 'frame hitches during fast key input' is not shown, and the cost is risk on weaker machines. The count includes the outline and composer passes (game.ts:450-451), the same way RULES measures it.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-arcade-rush-play/v6-fps.mjs log: fps 60.0, dc 1416, draw ≈ 4.9 ms over 8 s real time
findings.fix_correction: Verify with THROTTLE=4 node tools/perf.mjs on a mid laptop, as NEXT_STEPS.md asks, in addition to the drawCalls check.

findings.title: Rush cabinet stories name the fault, which removes the diagnosis
findings.problem: Rush stories hand over the diagnosis that the story Arcade made players earn: 'Someone fitted a block across the LED.', 'Right blocks, but the LED went in backwards.', 'The chain socket is empty.' Combined with 'backwards' starting with the correct chain, about 40% of cabinets need no reasoning. The house rule (PROGRESS l.248, A8) is that messages say why, never the fix. Symptoms ('The fuse keeps clicking', 'Stays dark', 'Barely glowing') would let the player read the board and the meter, which is the skill Rush should drill.
evidence: mockups/review5/shots/arcade-rush-play-73-space-jump-at-bench.jpg (panel: 'Right blocks, but the LED went in backwards. It stays dark.')
findings.fix:
Make the stories in `rushJob` symptom-only:
- across: 'The fuse keeps clicking.'
- backwards: 'Stays dark, even with fresh blocks.' Start it with a near-miss chain.
- hot: 'Too bright, and it smells warm.'
- dim: 'Barely glowing.'
- empty: 'The fuse clicks the moment it's switched on.'
findings.verify: Read each rush story: none names the part or the fix. logic.test asserts the story doesn't match /across|backwards|empty/.
findings.verify_reason: The code confirms it. The stories for 'across' ('Someone fitted a block across the LED.'), 'backwards' ('Right blocks, but the LED went in backwards.') and 'empty' ('The chain socket is empty.') name the fault (logic.ts:213-217). 'hot' and 'dim' are already symptom-only, so those two need no change. The proposed 'empty' text ('the fuse clicks the moment it's switched on') is electrically truthful: an empty chain is wire only, which trips the fuse (logic.ts:151).
extra_evidence: src/stations/arcade/logic.ts:151 (wire-only → fuse trips, so the proposed symptom text is truthful)

notes.fun:
What works: the core bench loop is readable and snappy once learned. With a known answer a cabinet takes about 5 s (2 s to read, 1–7 keys, a 2 s play test), the meter, the LED glow and the ★ zone make a hit feel good, and the 'Elegant ★' toast with the bell is a tidy beat. Something physical happens in the first second if the player wants it (I threw a cone at 1.2 s, fastestProp 7.9 m/s, so DR-03 passes).

What doesn't work:
- **The grade:** an idle 3 minutes grades A and records a best A, because the time axis is always 180 s ≤ 190. Cost punishes throughput: 32 elegant cabinets grade C on cost.
- **Variety:** generated cabinets are LED-only single faults collapsing to about nine answers. There's no escalation, no queue or stakes, and the physical cabinet never changes.
- **The payoff:** the kid, the cabinet and the confetti are all outside the bench camera, so the payoff of every loop is a text pill.
- **The clock:** it hard-cuts an order at 1.8/2 s.
- **Chaos:** throwing the tray onto the bench is punished (damage 1, cost 10, not accepted). The room has no cable, so AGENTS 4 has nothing to say here.

The mode currently feels like a timed quiz bolted onto a room, not a Good Job rush.
notes.playability:
Clean route: spawn → tray → bench takes about 6.5 s of game time, and the lanes are clear. The tray can't be wedged (thrown into the storeroom corner and against the shelf, it stays reachable and the prompt finds it), and the audit is clean (`g.audit(.02)` = []). No console errors in 9 scripts.

Problems:
- **Phone:** the bench is unplayable at 390×844. Two bins and the sign-off stamp are off-screen, there are no touch controls and the badges are keyboard keys (P0, A12 still open).
- **R at the bench** reloads the run instantly. Space jumps Pip while seated.
- **Live swaps:** every swap with the power on trips the fuse, because lifting a block leaves 'wire only' for more than 0.15 s, so the trip bonus is unattainable for experimenters.
- **Prompt:** 'P Power on' on a broken start counts a mistake and a trip immediately (A7 still open).
- **Occlusion:** the storeroom shelf hides Pip and the tray with no fade.
- **Performance:** draw calls are 1416, 1491 and 1178 against a budget of 250.

Leaving the bench mid-soak is forgiving (the soak continues), and Enter before the pass is safely rejected.
notes.clarity:
The objective card (3 dots, current step) and the one-line prompt mostly agree with the state.

Problems:
- **Feedback lag:** the card lags about 0.8 s at sit-down. Toasts outlive the arrangement they describe: a 100 Ω board shows TRIP with 'Nothing in the chain limits the current', which misleads.
- **Hidden damage:** bench mistakes don't show in the HUD damage tally until the result card.
- **Clocks:** the ring measures 240 s while the clock counts 180 s, and the panel repeats the seconds.
- **Result card:** it still leads with a meaningless 3:00 A row, with orders served as a caption.
- **Key hints:** bins, lever and stamp have no keycaps, so the 12-key layout is learned by hovering.
- **Word count:** about 40–45 words outside the monitor at the bench: card, panel story and rows, prompt, Esc chip, board legends.
- **Floating sign:** the STOREROOM sign still floats.

A new player can tell 'carry the tray' from the marker cone and the card, and 'sit at the bench' from the prompt. But they can't tell from the scene that powering a broken board costs them, or that swapping live is a trap.
notes.teaching: Not my primary dimension, but noted. Rush reuses the station's truthful model (I = (V − Vf) ÷ R, series/parallel, the PTC fuse), and the elegant zone rewards least current. Stories that name the fault ('went in backwards', 'fitted a block across') and 'backwards' starting with the correct chain remove the diagnosis. The answers become a lookup table after about 5 cabinets. The stale trip toast teaches a false cause (100 Ω 'trips' 9 V). Brute force is effectively free, since mistakes never affect the always-A grade, so DR-38 fails in Rush.
notes.models:
Out of scope for this key. Seen in passing:
- The play-test kid is still a realistic human (DR-60, known).
- The STOREROOM plaque floats at y 2.1 (DR-72, known).
- The tray clips into the shelf boxes when it comes to rest against the shelf (shot 58).
- The back-wall cabinets accumulate glow sprites per sign-off.
- The bench cabinet marquee correctly retitles per rush job (CLAW, DANCE).

rechecked: AR1 / R3A N4 (rush countdown clock and count on the result card): PARTIAL.
